title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
Final page (section 55) of E420, 'Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi', Novi Commentarii 16 (1771/1772). It contains no new computation. It is a short historical and methodological closing remark.

Euler recalls the stages of the theory:
- Early variational problems sought a curve making ∫Z dx a maximum or minimum among all curves.
- Then came 'isoperimetric' problems, where the competing curves must have a fixed length. This is the origin of the name, from the Bernoulli brothers' quarrel of 1697–1701.
- These were generalised to fixing the value of an arbitrary integral ∫V dx.
- Finally, several integrals ∫V dx, ∫V' dx, ∫V'' dx, ... were fixed at once.

In modern terms: extremise J[y] = ∫Z(x,y,y',...) dx subject to K_i[y] = ∫V_i dx = c_i, for i = 1..m.

Euler notes that in his treatise (the Methodus inveniendi of 1744) he showed that all such problems reduce to the unconstrained problem of extremising ∫(Z + αV + βV' + γV'' + ...) dx, with constant α, β, γ, .... These constants are fixed afterwards by the constraint values. This is the multiplier rule for isoperimetric problems. The Euler–Lagrange equation of Z + Σ λ_i V_i, together with the m constraints, determines the extremal and the λ_i.

The page ends with the catchword 'DE', which belongs to the next article in the journal volume, not to E420.

Context: the preceding pages applied the new method to free problems with Z depending on p = y' and q = y''. The previous page integrated the case Z = q²/(1+p²)^{5/2} via a first integral Z − Qq = Ap + B. Section 55 indicates that the constrained case adds nothing new once the multiplier reduction is granted.
errors: No computational errors on this page.

Gap by modern standards: the multiplier rule is stated without proof and without the normality (non-degeneracy) condition. In abnormal cases a multiplier λ0 on Z is needed: λ0 Z + Σ λ_i V_i, the later Mayer/Bolza/Weierstrass refinement.

Saying the combined integral itself becomes 'maximum vel minimum' is loose. In general one only gets stationarity of ∫(Z + Σ λ_i V_i), and the combined functional need not be extremal among all curves.

ideas.what: Isoperimetric problems reduce to an unconstrained problem for Z + αV + βV' + ... with constant multipliers, for any number of integral constraints
ideas.modern_name: Euler's multiplier rule for isoperimetric problems (Lagrange multipliers in the calculus of variations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, Methodus inveniendi lineas curvas (1744), Ch. V–VI; the multiplier idea for finite constraints is generally attributed to Lagrange
ideas.where_published: E65 Methodus inveniendi (1744); also discussed in Euler's later variational papers and in Institutiones calculi integralis vol. 3, Appendix

ideas.what: Historical remark on the origin of the name 'isoperimetric problem' and its successive generalisations
ideas.modern_name: History of the isoperimetric problem (Bernoulli brothers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jakob and Johann Bernoulli (1697–1701); systematised by Euler
ideas.where_published: E65 and Euler's earlier isoperimetric papers (e.g., E27, E56)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a closing historical summary restating Euler's well-known 1744 isoperimetric multiplier rule. It is thoroughly documented in histories of the calculus of variations (Goldstine, Fraser, Carathéodory's introductions in Opera omnia I.24/I.25). Nothing new here.
transcription_corrections: The transcription matches the image. The final 'DE' is a catchword for the next article in the volume, not part of E420's text.
'quaeratur' is printed as 'quaeratur' (the image shows 'quaeratur'), and 'val r' in the image is 'valor' with a broken letter. The transcription correctly reads 'valor'.
